fields.site: Corbin Valley operations center, Conference Room B
fields.cyclePosition: Year 2 of the 3-year cycle that began 2025-01-01 (ends 2027-12-31)
fields.description: A release from Line 4 into Harlan Creek, 20 miles above a municipal water intake. The IMT notified the agencies, activated the OSRO, ranked the sensitive areas and prepared an in-situ burn request.
fields.worstCaseDischarge: Yes: the plan's worst case discharge for the river crossing segment (2,800 barrels)

objectives.text: Coordination of internal organization personnel with responsibility for response
Annual review of the transition from a local team to a regional, national and international team as appropriate
Ability to coordinate response activity with the National Response System infrastructure (if its personnel are not participating, show knowledge of the coordination)
Ability to access information in the Area Contingency Plan on the location of sensitive areas, resources available in the area and unique conditions of the area
Simulation of a worst case discharge scenario (at least one IMT exercise in each triennial cycle)

For any chemical or biological countermeasure or in-situ burn in the plan, prepare and submit a request, usage and monitoring plan; each countermeasure in the plan is exercised during the triennial cycle

components.name: Operate within the response management system

fields.evaluation: Facilitated review by the exercise design team against the objectives above. Objective F was only discussed; the regional team was not on the call.
lessons: The after-hours call list for the OSRO was out of date.
The water intake contact was reached after 40 minutes; keep a direct number in the plan.
The countermeasure request needed the monitoring plan attached before it could be sent.
fields.certificationStatement: I certify that this exercise was conducted as described, that its objectives were evaluated, and that this record is accurate.
fields.certifierName: D. Alvarez, Director of Emergency Response
fields.retention: Keep this record and the exercise materials for three years; records location: as indicated in the response plan. Documentation is usually completed within 60 days of the exercise. This is generic guidance, not legal advice; the plan holder and the regulator decide what satisfies the plan.
fields.edition: Objectives follow the 2016 National Preparedness for Response Exercise Program (PREP) Guidelines, version 2016.1.
